nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of MSN-WO3
nodes.procedure: The self-supported mirror-symmetric nanoarray constructed by c-axis-oriented single-crystalline WO3 nanoneedles (namely MSN-WO3) on NF was synthesized by a simple hydrothermal method with ammonium metatungstate (AMT) as a tungsten source using 0.6 mmol AMT (see details in the ESI†).

unit_operations.name: Hydrothermal reaction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: synthesized by a simple hydrothermal method with ammonium metatungstate (AMT) as a tungsten source using 0.6 mmol AMT

nodes.source_text: A mirror-symmetric Ru/WO3-x nanoarray... was fabricated via a three-step synthesis procedure... MSN-WO3 on NF was synthesized by a simple hydrothermal method with ammonium metatungstate (AMT) as a tungsten source... Further increasing the AMT amount (0.6 mmol) mainly promotes the c-axis-oriented lateral growth

nodes.name: H2/Ar heat-reduction
nodes.procedure: Then followed by a heat-reduction treatment in an H2/Ar mixed atmosphere, oxygen-deficient MSN-WO3 was obtained (namely MSN-WO3-x).

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples display clear diffraction peaks of hexagonal WO3 (JCPDS No. 85-2460). No obvious diffraction peak related to Ru NCs observed in Ru/MSN-WO3-x due to small size/low content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structures of various samples were examined by X-ray diffraction (XRD). As shown in Fig. 2a, all samples display clear diffraction peaks of hexagonal WO3 (JCPDS No. 85-2460).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/MSN-WO3-x shows uniformly distributed Ru nanoclusters with average size of 1.1 nm. MSN-WO3-x nanoneedles became highly porous after oxygen extraction while maintaining c-axis-oriented single-crystalline nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The average size of the Ru NCs on Ru/MSN-WO3-x is about 1.1 nm (the inset of Fig. 2n). Both lattice spacings corresponding to hexagonal WO3 and hexagonal Ru can be clearly observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringes confirm c-axis orientation of MSN-WO3 nanoneedles along (002) direction. Ru/MSN-WO3-x shows lattice spacings for both hexagonal WO3 and Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Each of these nanoneedles is single-crystalline, with the same (002) growth direction... Both lattice spacings corresponding to hexagonal WO3 and hexagonal Ru can be clearly observed in the HRTEM images.

nodes.characterization_summary: Parallel array structure of MSN-WO3 confirmed. MSN-WO3-x maintains c-axis-oriented single-crystalline nature with lattice fringes parallel in (100) direction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HADDF-STEM) image shows the parallel array structure of MSN-WO3... the lattice fringes of different nanoneedles from the same nanoarray are still highly parallel.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru mass loading in Ru/MSN-WO3-x is 0.21 mg cm^-2, W loading on NF is 35.4 mg cm^-2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The mass loading of Ru in Ru/MSN-WO3-x was determined to be 0.21 mg cm^-2 while that of W on NF was determined to be 35.4 mg cm^-2 by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES).

nodes.characterization_summary: W 4f XPS of MSN-WO3 shows W(VI) peaks at 35.38 eV (W 4f7/2) and 37.48 eV (W 4f5/2). MSN-WO3-x shows additional W(V) peaks at 33.78 eV and 36.28 eV confirming oxygen vacancies. Ru 3p XPS of Ru/MSN-WO3-x shows Ru(0) peaks at 461.9 eV (Ru 3p3/2) and 484.0 eV (Ru 3p1/2) with positive shift vs commercial Ru/C indicating strong metal-support interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the fitted W 4f XPS spectra (Fig. 2b), MSN-WO3 displays two main peaks at 35.38 eV and 37.48 eV, which correspond well to the W 4f7/2 and W 4f5/2 of W(VI)... In the fitted Ru 3p XPS spectra (Fig. 2c), a pair of peaks at 461.9 eV and 484.0 eV can be assigned to Ru 3p3/2 and Ru 3p1/2 of Ru(0).
